fuel_consumption.source_quote: Based on projected 2003 fuel usage, such an increase would result in an increase to aircraft fuel expense of approximately $205 million in 2003, net of fuel hedge instruments outstanding at December 31, 2002

instrument_type_details.notes: American enters into jet fuel, heating oil and crude swap and option contracts. Note 9 reports 1.7 billion gallons of fuel products hedged at December 31, 2002 across 2003-2005 coverage years. Fair value of agreements totaled $212 million (amount company would receive to terminate).

warnings: Total fuel consumption in gallons not explicitly stated; only dollar-based market risk sensitivity provided.
The 1.7 billion gallons mentioned in Note 9 is the total notional volume across all hedge contracts outstanding (2003-2005), not annual consumption.
This filing covers AMR Corporation (parent); American Airlines, Inc. (CIK 6201) is the principal operating subsidiary.
Credit rating constraints noted: 'The Company's credit rating has limited its ability to enter into certain types of fuel hedge contracts.'
